name: Nun
overview: Nun was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, known primarily as the father of Joshua. His role is briefly noted in Scripture, highlighting his connection to a significant biblical figure. Beyond this familial link, there are no additional details or notes about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Nun, also rendered as Non, means 'fish,' which symbolizes fertility and productivity. This meaning reflects a Hebrew understanding of the name but was not given directly by God. Both forms of the name appear in Scripture in reference to the same individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Nun as the father of Joshua, a key leader of Israel. Additionally, he is noted as a descendant of Ephraim, linking him to one of the tribes of Israel. No other family relationships are recorded beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Nun's primary significance in the biblical narrative is as the father of Joshua, who succeeded Moses as the leader of Israel. This connection places Nun within the lineage of God's chosen people and highlights his role in the continuity of God's plan for Israel. While Nun himself is not a prominent figure, his position as Joshua's father situates him within the unfolding story of God's covenant faithfulness.
